correctness.rationale: The stationary current is constant and integrable (bounded speeds and integrable densities), hence zero. Solving the flux ODE gives a positive even analytic density with exponential tails. Its derivative on x>0 has the sign of A−H_q(ux). The log derivative of h_q is 2q/sinh(2qy)+3 tanh(y)−coth(y); the first term decreases in q, and h_2=2/(1−tanh^4(y)) strictly increases on the positive half-line. Thus H_q strictly increases to infinity for q≤2, including strict central maximality when A=H_q(0). For every fixed q>2, taking gamma_0=gamma_1=b, v_1=u=1 and v_0=L>max(1,3/[q(q²−4)]) makes H_q/b decrease locally at zero by the quadratic Taylor coefficient. Choosing b between the reciprocals of the two levels forces derivative signs −,+,− on the positive half-line; analyticity makes the sign-changing extrema strict, and reflection gives the additional peak. The q=5/2 witness independently gives H(0)=126/125 and H(atanh(1/3))=(43281−9072√2)/31000<1, by 2·9072²−12281²=13779407>0.
residual_risks: The bundled script was not executed in this review; its finite checks are not the continuum proof. No exact mode ceiling above q=2 or dynamic convergence claim was assessed.
